title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 56 (Transfer and Transmission of Securities)

content.overview: Section 56 governs transfer and transmission of securities. A company shall not register a transfer of securities unless a proper instrument of transfer in the prescribed form, duly stamped, dated and executed by or on behalf of the transferor and the transferee, is delivered to the company within the prescribed period, along with the certificate. Transmission by operation of law (death, insolvency, etc.) is recognised without an instrument of transfer. Time limits apply for delivery of certificates after transfer or allotment.
content.glance: Proper instrument of transfer required for registration; transmission by operation of law without instrument; certificate delivery timelines; penalties for default.
content.study: A company shall not register a transfer of securities of the company unless a proper instrument of transfer, in such form as may be prescribed, duly stamped, dated and executed by or on behalf of the transferor and the transferee and specifying the name, address and occupation (if any) of the transferee, has been delivered to the company by the transferor or the transferee within a period of sixty days from the date of execution, along with the certificate relating to the securities. Where the instrument is lost or not delivered within time, the company may register on such terms as to indemnity as the Board may think fit. Nothing in the section prejudices transmission of securities by operation of law. The company must deliver certificates of securities allotted or transferred within prescribed periods. Current-law framing: identify transfer vs transmission; for transfer, test instrument, stamping, delivery and certificate; for transmission, apply operation-of-law route.

sections.heading: Transfer — Instrument
sections.body: Registration of transfer requires a proper prescribed instrument, duly stamped, dated and executed by transferor and transferee, delivered with the certificate within the prescribed period.

sections.heading: Lost Instrument / Late Delivery
sections.body: Board may register on indemnity terms where the instrument is lost or not delivered in time.

sections.heading: Transmission
sections.body: Transmission by operation of law (e.g. death, insolvency) does not require an instrument of transfer.

sections.heading: Certificate Delivery
sections.body: Certificates must be delivered within the statutory periods after allotment or transfer; default attracts penalty.

examples.title: Valid transfer
examples.body: A duly stamped and executed transfer form is delivered with the share certificate within sixty days. The company may register the transfer under s. 56.

examples.title: Transmission on death
examples.body: On the death of a member, the legal representative seeks registration by transmission. No instrument of transfer is required under s. 56.

hypotheticals.question: Is an oral agreement enough to compel registration of a share transfer?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 56 requires a proper instrument of transfer in the prescribed form, duly stamped and executed, delivered with the certificate (subject to indemnity for loss).

distinctions.title: Transfer/transmission (s. 56) vs refusal of registration (s. 58)
distinctions.right: When registration may be refused and Tribunal appeal

misconceptions.trap: Transmission also needs a transfer form.
misconceptions.correction: Section 56 expressly preserves transmission by operation of law without an instrument of transfer.

cases.name: Salomon v. A. Salomon & Co. Ltd.
cases.facts: Properly incorporated company challenged as indistinct from controller.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Registered company is a separate legal person.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 56 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Classify transfer or transmission. II. For transfer, test instrument, stamp, delivery, certificate. III. For transmission, apply operation of law. IV. Check certificate timelines. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Instrument or transmission facts; timelines; certificate delivery; precise relief.
